items.title: Pennsylvania mom's $4,500 ambulance bill exposes loophole in surprise billing law - cbsnews.com
items.reason: The article documents a specific gap in No Surprises Act coverage (ambulance services) and illustrates balance-billing enforcement challenges, which directly impacts revenue-cycle teams' understanding of the law's scope and limitations.
items.summary: A Pennsylvania family received a $4,500 surprise bill for an ambulance transport, highlighting that ground ambulance services fall outside the No Surprises Act's balance-billing protections because they are not classified as healthcare providers under the law. While the No Surprises Act prohibits surprise bills from emergency room visits and in-network facilities, ambulance operators are excluded from these protections, leaving patients vulnerable to out-of-network charges. This loophole affects revenue-cycle teams by creating coverage gaps they must navigate and underscores the need for patients and providers to understand which emergency services are actually protected by the law.
